exclusion_reason: The contention fixture runs deterministically under N workers over the cooperative scheduler model with byte-reproducible guest-visible state and zero lost wakeup, but the production target — a real SharedArrayBuffer-backed Worker pool with true cross-core parallelism — is not deployed on the run surface, so that deployment leg stays red.
promotion_trigger: Promote to passing when the contention fixture is deterministic with no lost wakeup on a real SharedArrayBuffer-backed Worker pool across repeated runs and a second machine.
expected_failing_assertion: The reproducible schedule is a deterministic cooperative model; no SharedArrayBuffer-backed Worker pool executes the fixture across real cores, so the cross-core deployment cannot be measured.
active_gate_evidence: test/thread.test.mjs drives runContentionFixture: N workers contend on an interlocked counter and a critical-section-guarded counter and hand a token around an auto-reset event; it asserts both counters reach the expected total, that the guest-state hash and the schedule hash are byte-reproducible across repeated runs, that the guest-state hash is identical across worker counts (1 and 8) with lost_wakeup_count zero and no deadlock, and that is_worker_backed is false so no real cross-core runtime is claimed.
procedure: Run the lock and atomic-contention fixture under the declared worker count.
Repeat the run and compare guest-visible state for determinism.
Assert every waiter wakes exactly once.
pass_criterion: Guest-visible state is deterministic across repeated run.
